title: Why NPS’s Lock-in is a Feature for Retirement Savings
description: The National Pension System (NPS) has specific lock-in periods designed to ensure funds are preserved for retirement. This lock-in acts as "good friction," pr.

faq.q: What is the primary purpose of the NPS lock-in?
faq.a: The primary purpose is to ensure that funds contributed to NPS are preserved specifically for retirement, preventing premature withdrawals that could jeopardise long-term financial security. It acts as a deliberate barrier against impulsive decisions.

faq.q: Can I withdraw all my money from NPS before retirement?
faq.a: No, you cannot. If you exit NPS before age 60 (after 5 years), you must annuitise at least 80% of your corpus. Only 20% can be withdrawn as a taxable lump sum. This stringent rule reinforces its retirement-focused nature.

faq.q: Are there any situations where partial withdrawals are allowed from NPS?
faq.a: Yes, partial withdrawals of up to 25% of your own contributions are allowed after three years, for specific purposes like higher education, marriage, house purchase, or critical illness. A maximum of three such withdrawals are permitted during the entire tenure.

faq.q: How does the NPS lock-in benefit me financially?
faq.a: The lock-in ensures your money remains invested for the long term, allowing it to benefit fully from compounding. This disciplined approach helps in accumulating a much larger retirement corpus compared to more liquid instruments where funds might be withdrawn frequently.

faq.q: Is the lump sum withdrawal at maturity taxable?
faq.a: No, if you withdraw 60% of your corpus as a lump sum at age 60 (or superannuation), the entire amount is tax-exempt. The remaining 40% used for annuity purchase provides a taxable income during retirement.

faq.q: Can I change my investment strategy within NPS despite the lock-in?
faq.a: Yes, NPS offers flexibility. You can switch between different Pension Fund Managers (PFMs) and also change your asset allocation (e.g., from aggressive equity to more conservative debt) without any tax implications. This allows you to adapt your strategy over your investment horizon.

faq.q: Does my employer's contribution to NPS also have a lock-in?
faq.a: Yes, all contributions to the Tier I NPS account, whether by you or your employer, are subject to the same lock-in rules and withdrawal restrictions until maturity or specific partial withdrawal conditions are met.
